concerns.text: T105's verification requires records 'conforming to contracts/experiment_log.schema.yaml', but that schema makes consensus_gap_score a required field, and scores are only computed in T109 ('writing scores back into the logs'). As ordered, T105's acceptance gate is unachievable at its position — the consumer of the scores (schema validation) is placed before the producer (T109). Either move score computation into T105/T106, or restate T105's verification to check only the fields the runner produces (e.g., status, injected_state, llm_output) and defer full schema validation to T112.

T112 validates data/processed/experiment_logs.json against experiment_log.schema.yaml and gates on schema_valid being true. Since T109 mutates the logs (writes scores back), T112 is correctly ordered after T109, but the T105 verification (see prior concern) duplicates this check prematurely. Consolidate: make T112 the single schema-validation gate for experiment logs and remove the schema claim from T105's verification to avoid two tasks gating on the same unmet condition.

T112 pairs classifier_training_data.json with contracts/trajectory.schema.yaml, but T103's training records (turn_text/label/confidence_score) are not ConflictTrajectory objects; no task produces a schema those records can validate against. This is a producer/consumer mismatch: either add a training-record schema to contracts/ or restrict T112 to experiment_logs.json vs experiment_log.schema.yaml.
